- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1 → +1), model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–4% for next 2–3 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is mixed (e.g., 1.00 and -1.00 alternating); apply +2% bias to forecast mean for next 5 days.
- If last 3–5 days show mean reversion (e.g., 75–85 range), model overreacts to recent highs; apply -3% correction to forecast for next 3 days.
- When sentiment is positive and model forecast is below 75, add +3% to forecast for next 2 days; if above 85, reduce by 2% for next 2 days.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 1–2 days; adjust forecast 1 day ahead if sentiment changes direction.
